answers.explanation: Application, Host-to-Host Transport, Internet, and Network Access.
In TCP/IP an application handles its own presentation and sessions.
It matches OSI layer 3, the network layer.
It deliberately says nothing about hardware. Any network that can carry an IP datagram will do.
A switch is a layer 2 device. A hub (layer 1) just repeats the signal, and a router (layer 3) uses IP addresses.
Hubs and repeaters work on raw signals. They don't understand addresses at all.
Routers are layer 3 devices. They read the destination IP address in the packet header.
"Layer 2" and "layer 3" almost always mean OSI's numbers, even on TCP/IP networks.
It builds the whole stack to send, and unpacks it to receive.
